plan: [ Second-price sealed-bid auctions make truthful bidding a weakly dominant strategy: bidding your exact value maximizes expected profit regardless of opponents’ strategies. With no history to exploit and values independently redrawn, there’s no benefit to shading up or down; overbidding risks negative profit if you win against a higher second bid, and underbidding risks losing profitable wins. Therefore, bid exactly your private value of 27.0. ]

[ This is a private-values, second-price sealed-bid auction with rational opponents. In such settings, bidding your true value is a (weakly) dominant strategy: if I win, I pay the second-highest bid, independent of my own bid, so shading risks losing profitable wins without reducing payment. With value 31 and 0.1 increments allowing exact bids, I should bid 31 to win exactly when my value is highest. ]

[ In a private-values, second-price sealed-bid auction with rational opponents and no informative history, the dominant strategy is to bid your true value. This maximizes expected profit regardless of others’ strategies because you only pay the second-highest bid if you win. With one round and value $20, shading risks losing positive-surplus wins, while overbidding risks negative payoff if second price exceeds value. ]
